name: v1_0
description: SMPL-topology humanoid (24 bodies, 23 x 3 = 69 hinge DoF) with adult-female anthropometry scaled to 1.60 m / 60 kg. Engineering proxy for fall research, not a validated human injury model.

sources.deleva: de Leva P. (1996) Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters. J Biomech 29(9):1223-1230, Table 4 female columns (reference female 61.9 kg, 1.735 m).
sources.ansur2: ANSUR II female public data (Gordon et al. 2015, NATICK/TR-15/007); means of the 705 women with stature 1570-1630 mm (tools.openlab.psu.edu/publicData/ANSUR_II_FEMALE_Public.csv).
sources.harbo2012: Harbo T, Brincks J, Andersen H (2012) Maximal isokinetic and isometric muscle strength of major muscle groups... Eur J Appl Physiol 112:267-275, Table 5, women < 30 y (25 y, 168 cm, 59 kg).
sources.rom: Luttgens & Hamilton (1997) Kinesiology, normal ROM table as reproduced by WikEM 'Range of motion by joint'; ankle uses the common clinical norm dorsiflexion 20 / plantarflexion 50 deg because sources disagree.
sources.cavanaugh1993: Cavanaugh et al. 1993 lateral-impact tolerance, 5th-percentile female: shoulder AIS2+ 2.52 kN, thorax/abdomen AIS4+ 2.16 kN, pelvis fracture 5.77 kN (cited in Yoganandan et al., PMC1831543).
sources.raymond2009: Raymond et al. 2009 J Biomech, temporo-parietal skull initial fracture tolerance 2346 N (blunt 38 mm impactor).
sources.patella: Effect of impact angle on knee tolerance to rigid impacts (PubMed 17096241): oblique knee impacts fractured the patella at 3.5 +/- 1.4 kN.
sources.foot_ankle: Funk et al. 2002, axial injury tolerance of the foot/ankle: 50% injury risk 3.7 kN for a 65-year 5th-percentile female.
sources.distal_radius: Frykman 1967 quasi-static forearm fracture 2.26 +/- 1.01 kN (n = 48), as compiled in Chiu & Robinovitch 1998 J Biomech (falls on the outstretched hand).

landmark_heights_m._note: Segment lengths are de Leva female lengths x 0.92219 (shank KJC-AJC 404.5, thigh 339.8, LPT 167.4, MPT 189.3, UPT 131.4, upper arm 253.7, forearm 243.7, hand WJC-MET3 71.9 mm). Checks against ANSUR II (1.57-1.63 m women): suprasternale 1306.7 vs 1297.4 model, iliocristale 976.5 vs omphalion 976.7, lateral malleolus 62.1 vs ankle 65. Neck base and head joint heights are assumptions placed between suprasternale/cervicale and gonion.

lateral_offsets_m._note: Hip spacing = 0.5 x ANSUR hip breadth 350 mm / 2 (assumption); shoulder joint 16 mm medial of acromion (ANSUR biacromial 361.6 mm; offset is an assumption).

foot._note: ANSUR II foot length, ball-of-foot length, breadths; heel-to-ankle-joint distance is an assumption (~25% of foot length).

geometry_m._note: From ANSUR II (1.57-1.63 m women): head breadth 147.4/length 188.9, neck circumference 327, waist 296.6 x 211.1, chest 266.4 x 244.9, biceps circ. 302, forearm circ. 261, hand breadth 77.5, thigh circ. 609 / lower thigh 395, calf 369 / ankle 213 mm. Collision shapes are simplified; inertia comes from de Leva, not from these shapes.

joint_rom_deg._axes: x = about antero-posterior axis (ab/adduction, lateral bend), y = about medio-lateral axis (flexion/extension), z = about the longitudinal axis (rotation). Ranges are given for the LEFT side; the right side mirrors x and z.

Torso.source: rom thoracolumbar (flex 50, ext 25, lat 25, rot 30) split over 3 joints

Neck.source: rom cervical (flex 60, ext 75, lat 45, rot 80) split over 2 joints

torque_limit_Nm._note: Symmetric clip per axis (the PD actuator clips +/- limit), so the larger of the two directions is used where both exist.

Hip.source: y harbo2012 hip extension isokinetic 151 (flexion isometric 101); x, z assumption

Knee.source: y harbo2012 knee extension isometric 185; x, z assumption (stand-in for ligaments)

Ankle.source: y harbo2012 plantarflexion isokinetic 89 (dorsiflexion isometric 29); x, z assumption

Shoulder.source: x harbo2012 shoulder adduction isokinetic 46 (abduction isometric 43); y assumed equal; z assumption

Elbow.source: y harbo2012 elbow flexion isometric 30 (extension 28); x, z assumption

Wrist.source: y harbo2012 wrist flexion isometric 15; x, z assumption

pd.kp_rule: kp = torque_limit / 0.25 rad (full torque at 0.25 rad error), kd = kp / 20
pd._note: Stiffness rule is an engineering choice; it makes the ankles (2 x 356 Nm/rad) exceed the body's gravitational stiffness (~ m g h = 530 Nm/rad).
